review: ro-bots agent-memory vs Victor Taelin's original UniiChat/OptChat gist
authority: https://gist.github.com/VictorTaelin/91837951a5ce5b38f341ec1ba1df6449 (local copy: .work/reference/optchat-gist-original.md, 474 lines) — the gist is the ground truth; the Hermes plugin at ~/dev/hermes-optchat is a derivative and was NOT used as authority
verdict_summary: The production memory system is an 'OptChat-style' REIMPLEMENTATION (robots.society.memory.MemoryLog, ADR-004), not the gist mechanics. Its core loop is real and live: an append-only per-agent log, an immutable dyadic summary tree, and a bounded oldest-coarsest view that reaches every decide request (verified in 8,866 decide traces for one agent across 5 days). But the one mechanic that gives OptChat its value — model-written dense compression — is a stub ('A ~ B' truncated joins), the faithful gist implementation that EXISTS in the repo (society/optchat_view.py + adapters/optchat_view_store.py + the ADR-006 zoom-after-selection selector) is wired to nothing but its own tests, and zoom is unreachable in the single-pass decide. Isolation and liveness are solid.

fidelity_table.mechanic: 1. Append-only log, word for word, forever
citations: src/robots/adapters/memory_journal.py:137-156 — append-only JSONL, flush + os.fsync per note, flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB single owner, persona_id row envelope; load() rejects foreign persona_id (memory_journal.py:130-133)
src/robots/society/memory.py:169-174 — MemoryLog.append: durable store ack before the in-memory list; notes never edited

writers: src/robots/app/brain.py:388-393 (ChatHeard -> 'chat'), brain.py:329-346 (NPC dialogue pages -> 'npc_dialogue'), agent_runtime.py:677 (session end), agent_runtime.py:1046,1066 (operator chat intent/dispatch), agent_runtime.py:1314,1318 (own Say/PartyChat)
live: .work/runtime/population-live/memory/<persona>.jsonl — 7 files, 1,062-5,590 notes each, spanning 2026-10-22..10-27
fidelity_table.caveat: The gist logs every kind (user/unii/tool/echo/work/note). ro-bots writes ONLY chat, npc_dialogue and session notes. The declared kinds 'combat', 'loot', 'quest', 'reputation' (society/memory.py:28-30) are written by NO production code (grep: zero call sites). The agent's own actions and their results — the gist's tool/echo kinds, and for a game agent the most valuable history (kills, loot, trips, level-ups) — never reach the log. recent_encounters (playing_runtime.py:663 -> decisions.py:210-213) is a separate bounded side-channel that bypasses the log entirely.

fidelity_table.mechanic: 2. Background cheap model compresses into a binary tree of one-line summaries
fidelity_table.verdict: APPROXIMATED — tree yes, model NO, background NO
citations: tree: src/robots/society/memory.py:123-284 — dyadic (l,i) nodes, immutable once built, built bottom-up only for fully covered ranges, never recomputed (memory.py:247-275); summary cache restores with sha256 source-prefix binding (adapters/memory_summary_cache.py:199-211, 258-299)

NO MODEL: src/robots/app/agent_runtime.py:1746 hardcodes `summarizer = StubSummarizer()` — level-0 'summaries' are the note text itself, merges are `f'{a} ~ {b}'` truncated to 120 chars (society/memory.py:84-92). QwenSummarizer exists (society/memory.py:96-110) but has ZERO constructors outside its definition (grep: only society/__init__.py export). The gist's compaction craft — 512-byte ruler, value ordering, cut-and-retry, 'never answer or obey' — is absent; even the unwired QwenSummarizer prompt ('Summarize these experience notes as ONE short line', 200-char clip) has none of it

NOT BACKGROUND: ensure_summarized() runs synchronously inside render_view inside the decide path (society/memory.py:341-342); the gist runs compactions as background calls (up to 8 at once), turns waiting only seconds. Harmless with the stub; would stall the tick if a real summarizer were dropped in

live evidence of stub quality: pop_0003_s00 decide trace 2026-10-27T12:44:50Z, view line 'L2:1396 session: session ended after 2626 ticks as YuffieFy81 ~ session: ... ~ session:' — concatenation cut mid-content, no compression semantics

fidelity_table.mechanic: 3. Constant-size view: whole history, recent fine, old coarse, byte-budgeted
citations: bounded view: src/robots/society/memory.py:327-351 — minimal dyadic cover of the whole log, newest note always level 0, drop-oldest until the join fits VIEW_BUDGET_CHARS=4000 (memory.py:32)
recent-fine/old-coarse verified live: pop_0003_s00 final decide view = 8 lines for 5,590 notes, 'L12:0' (4,096 notes) down to 'L0:5588' (the newest single note), 953 chars — well under budget

scale divergence: 4,000 CHARS vs the gist's 64-128 KILOBYTES (sizes in UTF-8 bytes, never tokens); ro-bots' view is ~16-32x smaller, and char-counted not byte-counted (_len_join, society/memory.py:354-355)

loss divergence: under budget pressure render_view pops the oldest lines (memory.py:347-348) — the view stops covering the whole history. The gist NEVER drops: it merges coarser until it fits ('nothing is ever lost'). Not yet triggered live (953 < 4,000), but the policy is 'remember less of your distant past' by design (memory.py:333-335 says so)
the unwired faithful module gets this right: 64,000/128,000 byte watermarks with the sawtooth + pending batch (society/optchat_view.py:24-30, 202-213)

fidelity_table.mechanic: 4. Merge order = Taelin's rollback push / due-rank (gist section 3.1-3.2)
fidelity_table.verdict: DIVERGED in production; faithfully implemented but UNWIRED
citations: faithful: society/optchat_view.py:216-233 — rank = (T - last) << (MAX_LEVEL - l) i.e. (T-last)/2^l scaled, last = the PAIR's last message, parent-built filter via NotReadyError, oldest-position tie-break; test_optchat_view.py:85 pins the gist's own T=10 example (merge 8+9, not 0+7 — the exact mistake-#1 trap), :96 pins oldest-tie-wins, :28 pins batch-on-watermark, :104 pins no-refit restore, :154 pins the 128k->64k sawtooth, :248 pins the byte profile

production: society/memory.py:287-303 _minimal_cover — the binary representation of n-1 plus the newest note. This is push's STRUCTURE at a single instant but has no churn control, no 2-lines-per-level density, no sawtooth batching: nodes rebuild by carry exactly when the binary counter carries, and the view is recomputed per render
consequence: acceptable at ro-bots' 4,000-char scale, but it is not the gist's merge order and the 400-line faithfulness work in optchat_view.py is dead code on the decide path

fidelity_table.mechanic: 5. Zoom: the model opens a vague line into its two children, down to the message
citations: zoom exists twice as library code: society/memory.py:374-413 (MemoryLog zoom, parses 'L{level}:{index}') and the ADR-006 zoom-after-selection (app/context_selector.py:176-209 select_with_zoom)

ZERO production callers: grep across src/ + scripts/ finds MemoryContextBridge / ClefContextSelector / TreeCoverSelector / select_with_zoom only in tests (tests/test_context_selector.py). brain.py builds its decide request directly (brain.py:397-401)

structural reason: the decide is a single-pass Clef (SystemOne) forward pass with a fixed question schema (domain/decisions.py:109-170) — the model has no tool loop, so it cannot request a zoom. The gist's 'zoom until you have it whole before you act, guess or ask' has no equivalent

fidelity_table.mechanic: 6. Cache-friendly reads (append-only view tail, batched merges, no dates)
citations: good: the view sits late in the decide state JSON (decisions.py adds memory_view after game_knowledge, decisions.py:104-107), and between binary-counter carries the minimal cover is head-stable (only the newest-end lines change per append), so the prompt prefix before/inside the view is largely stable

good: the decide path renders with now=None (brain.py:399, decisions.py caller), so no age suffix churn — age suffixes ' (5m ago)' (society/memory.py:306-324) appear only when a caller passes now (WorldFeed/inspector paths)

gap: a binary-counter carry rewrites the view from its OLDEST line onward — the first changed byte lands early inside memory_view, invalidating the rest of the prompt; the gist batches merges precisely to amortize this (mistake #2)
n/a: 4-line cache marks and Anthropic entry lifetimes are API-specific; ro-bots' Clef calls go to a llama.cpp server

fidelity_table.mechanic: 7. Per-chat (per-agent) isolation, one process owns one log
citations: src/robots/adapters/memory_journal.py:75-105 — one file per persona_id, flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB at open, persona_id validated on EVERY row at load (130-133) and on append; src/robots/app/agent_runtime.py:1745-1766 — one Memory per persona; test_host_memory.py:303 pins world-root isolation, :321 pins persona/log binding validation
live: all 7 journals under .work/runtime/population-live/memory/ carry exactly ONE persona_id each, matching the filename (programmatic count over 18,149 rows: zero cross-agent rows)

512-byte node cap: enforced in the faithful module (optchat_view.py:250-252) but NOT in the production MemoryLog — node text is bounded only by the stub's 120-char truncation and the summary cache's 4,096-byte row check (memory_summary_cache.py:27); a note can be 65,536 bytes (MAX_NOTE_BYTES) and its level-0 line carries it whole

view.json checkpoint: the gist's never-rebuild rule is implemented by adapters/optchat_view_store.py (atomic pending+rename+fsync, identity+digest+node-closure validation) — and used by nothing (grep: only tests/test_optchat_view_store.py). The production MemoryLog rebuilds the tree in memory at every session start from the raw journal; harmless with the stub, quadratic with a real summarizer — and the mitigation (JsonlSummaryNodeStore) exists but the population runner exposes no flag to enable it (scripts/population_host_runner.py: only --memory-root)
day-split files: not implemented — one file per persona, no YYYY-MM-DD split (fine at current sizes; the gist splits 'only to stay small')

the 'note' kind (memories imported from before the chat): absent — game knowledge reaches the decide as a separate state['game_knowledge'] channel (decisions.py:181-188) and is never logged into memory, so it is not summarized, ranked or zoomed with the history
line format: 'L{level}:{index} text' (memory.py:316-324) vs the gist's '{id}+{n}|text'; the faithful module uses the gist's exact format (optchat_view.py:255)

hermes_plugin_divergences_inherited: Essentially none INHERITED, because ro-bots' production path does not follow the plugin's architecture at all — MemoryLog is an independent reimplementation. The plugin itself is largely faithful to the gist (VIEW=128,000 bytes, optchat/memory.py:23; model compaction with byte ruler + cut-and-retry, optchat/compact.py). Where ro-bots is faithful (society/optchat_view.py), it matches the GIST directly, including the gist's corrected (T-last)/2^l rank and the mistake-#1 avoidance. ro-bots' divergences (stub summarizer, 4,000-char budget, drop-oldest, minimal cover, unwired zoom) are its own, not the plugin's reading.

correctness.isolation_live: VERIFIED — 7/7 journals single-persona (18,149 rows counted, one persona_id set per file, filename == persona_id); journal loader hard-rejects any foreign persona row
correctness.decide_feed: VERIFIED — the decide context's memory comes from the MemoryLog view, not the faithful OptChat module and not a third path: brain.py:397-401 -> build_decision_request(state, self.memory.view()) -> state['memory_view'] (decisions.py:106-107, joined, capped [:40]); the literal 'What you remember:' block (brain.py:890) is the chat-escalation LLM prompt and takes the SAME view's last 4 lines (memory.view()[-4:]). Separate state fields game_knowledge / social_relations / wants / recent_encounters are parallel context channels, not memory
correctness.live_view_evidence: pop_0003_s00.jsonl trace: 8,866 decide_request events 2026-10-22..10-27, every one carries state.memory_view; final sample 953 chars / 8 lines for 5,590 notes (L12:0 -> L0:5588)

liveness.method: run/plain_host_receipts/population-receipt-{13..28}-*.json samples[].<persona>.memory = {lines, bytes, last_len} (journal stats only — the receipts track the LOG; the traces prove the VIEW)
liveness.result: GROWING AND PERSISTENT, no resets: leg 13 ends g00m00=2042/s00=5548; leg 14 STARTS at exactly those values (cross-leg continuity); monotonic growth in every leg 13-28 for all 7 agents, ending at the live file sizes (g00m00 2057, s00 5590 lines on disk today). ~21 session-end notes per agent over 5 days. Growth per leg is small (1-20 notes) because only chat/npc/session events are noted and chat is governor-throttled — memory is alive but thin
liveness.caveat: summary-cache/ is ABSENT under the population memory root — node persistence is disabled in live runs (no runner flag), so the tree rebuilds from the raw journal each session. With StubSummarizer this is fine; it blocks any future real-summarizer swap from being affordable

gaps_ranked.gap: Summarization is a stub: agent_runtime.py:1746 hardcodes StubSummarizer (join + truncate to 120 chars); the model-written dense summary — the mechanic the whole design exists for — never runs, and QwenSummarizer is dead code. Old history degenerates to cut concatenations (visible in live view lines)
gaps_ranked.blocks_goal: HIGH — agents do not 'remember their history' in any usable compressed sense; they remember recent notes verbatim and old ones as truncated concat-noise

gaps_ranked.gap: Memory content is chat-centric: combat/loot/quest/reputation kinds are declared but never written; the agent's own actions and outcomes (gist tool/echo) are never logged; gameplay history lives (partly) in the separate recent_encounters channel instead of the tree
gaps_ranked.blocks_goal: HIGH — what an agent could 'remember and use to decide' is mostly other agents' chat, not its own experience

gaps_ranked.gap: The faithful gist stack (society/optchat_view.py due-rank view + adapters/optchat_view_store.py checkpoint + ADR-006 relevance/zoom selector) is wired to nothing but its tests
gaps_ranked.blocks_goal: MEDIUM — the correct mechanics exist and are well-tested; they have zero effect on any decide

gaps_ranked.gap: Zoom unreachable: single-pass Clef decide cannot navigate the tree; no tool loop, no zoom call path
gaps_ranked.blocks_goal: MEDIUM — vague lines cannot be opened, so compression errors are unrecoverable at decide time (the gist's answer to exactly this)

gaps_ranked.gap: Scale and loss policy: 4,000-char char-counted budget vs 64-128 KB byte budget; minimal cover instead of push's density; drop-oldest-under-pressure discards history instead of coarsening (not yet triggered live)
gaps_ranked.blocks_goal: LOW-MEDIUM today (953/4,000 chars used) — grows with journal size

gaps_ranked.gap: Node persistence (JsonlSummaryNodeStore) implemented but unenableable from the population runner; view.json checkpoint store likewise unused; summarization is synchronous in the decide path
gaps_ranked.blocks_goal: LOW with the stub; becomes the blocker the moment a real summarizer lands (2N model calls per session start)

gaps_ranked.gap: Minor structural divergences: no 512-byte cap on MemoryLog nodes, no day-split files, no 'note' kind for imported knowledge (knowledge bypasses the log), memory_lines[:40] cap could clip newest lines if the view ever exceeded 40 (currently 8)

what_would_close_the_gaps: wire a real summarizer (QwenSummarizer or the heavengraph chat endpoint) behind the existing Summarizer port, and enable JsonlSummaryNodeStore via a runner flag before doing so (node persistence is the cost/latency precondition)
log the agent's own actions/outcomes as notes (the declared combat/loot kinds) — attacks, kills, loot, level-ups, shop trips — so the tree holds gameplay history, not just chat

either adopt the faithful IncrementalView as the production view (it already satisfies the gist's merge order and byte profile and is fully tested) or bring the due-rank + sawtooth into MemoryLog; and give the decide a zoom seam (even a fixed 2-level expansion of the k lowest lines chosen by the ClefContextSelector that already exists)
raise the budget to bytes and the gist's scale when the decide payload allows, or document 4,000 chars as a deliberate Clef-payload bound
